title: Forensic analysis shows latest Chinese LLMs were trained on Nvidia Blackwell B200/B300
author: K
text:
Xebec
Well-known member

An individual seems to have proven that the latest Chinese AI models (Deepseek-V4, Kimi K3, MiniMax-M3, and Ling-3.1) were trained used (export controlled) Nvidia Blackwell GPUs.

The post reads with a bit of sensationalism, but the take-away is that an AI model's base seed/starting values of it's weights are derived from a pattern established by the GPU it's trained on. You can therefore use the available open-weights (seeds) and information from different base GPUs to determine which GPU specifically was used to create/train a model.

"With some analysis of release schedules and model details, I estimate that the largest, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, used 2,000 to 3,000 Blackwell GPUs each. Clusters of this size cost on the order of $150 to $200 million each to buy, and across these labs alone would add up to more than half a billion dollars of export-controlled GPUs, not counting experimental compute or otherwise"

I have a major result to share.I’ve found conclusive forensic evidence that the top 4 Chinese AI labs—DeepSeek, Moonshot, MiniMax and Ant Group—have built their newest models on NVIDIA’s most advanced Blackwell chips, which are barred from export to China.This sounds insane,… pic.twitter.com/qlttvJsXG7— will depue (@willdepue) November 12, 2026
